title: The countable random graph: finite requests and one countable structure

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 64–65 (§6.1, Example 6.10: extension axioms and the binary-digit construction)

based_on.title: Model Theory: Cambridge Part III, Lent 2023
based_on.pages: 12–13 (§4, Proposition 4.8, Lemma 4.9 and Theorems 4.10–4.11; lectures by Barbina, notes by Tomczak)

summary: Construct one graph on the natural numbers that contains every finite graph, then recover its symmetries and its complete first-order theory from a finite extension rule.
abstract: Suppose we have chosen finitely many vertices and want a new vertex joined to some of them and to none of the others. A graph that always grants these requests contains every finite graph, and every finite symmetry of it extends to the whole countable structure. There is a particularly concrete example: two natural numbers are joined when the smaller number points to a nonzero binary digit of the larger. We prove that this graph grants every finite request and that the rule determines a unique countable graph up to isomorphism. Its first-order theory is complete and has quantifier elimination: a formula about a finite tuple can be replaced by a finite Boolean combination recording which coordinates are equal and which are joined.
